results.title: The Balcony in Shanghai Still Burns
results.overview: Sixteen years after leaving, a 1.5-generation Chinese-Canadian returns to her native city alone, seeking to reconnect with the place that once was home.

results.title: Whisper of Wall
results.overview: The suffering of the people in the Khmer Rouge’s prisons was undoubtedly immeasurable. Even decades after the fall of one of the cruellest regimes in history, messages and drawings remain etched on the walls of the former cells in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. It is as though the whispers of those lost forever remain, full of poetic defiance in the face of destruction.

results.title: Lassiguili
results.overview: This intimate documentary follows a bride-to-be who, according to Manding tradition, must spend the three days before her wedding in seclusion. Silence gives rise to questions: Was her mother afraid too? How can she be gentle, strong and true to herself? Between rituals and prayers, she enters a state of deep introspection and senses there is very much she has not been told.

results.title: Dotuk
results.overview: This apocalyptic cinéma vérité depicts the socio-economic situation in a remote Iranian village, which is lashed by violent sandstorms for 120 days a year. This is not a scene from the apocalypse, but the harsh reality for the inhabitants of Taj Mir in South Khorasan Province. Their sole source of income is hand-sewn “dotuk” dolls, a traditional ritual object that has become a commodity.

results.title: Murmurs in the Distance
results.overview: Murmurs in the Distance begins with an encounter with a gap: the absence of a substantial historical and visual record of the women’s protests of March 8, 1979 in Iran. Through photographs, recordings, testimonies, and archival fragments, three artists from another generation, living in different countries, search for what has been preserved, what has disappeared, and find their own reflections along the journey. The archive becomes both a source and a place for questioning. The short documentary Iranian Women’s Liberation Movement: Year Zero (1979) offers one of the few surviving visual traces of the protests, while testimonies bring other forms of memory into the present. Rather than reconstructing a complete history, the film stays with these fragments and silences, asking how an archive shapes what can be remembered, seen, and understood as history.

results.title: Under the Canopy
results.overview: A participatory document from the Andean-Amazonian foothills challenges the colonial narrative of the jungle as an uninhabited wilderness and the victim of natural resource exploitation. Indigenous peoples are taking an active role, combining the knowledge of their ancestors with modern technologies. They see the rainforest as a place where the human and the non-human, the rational and the mystical, meet.

results.title: Together as One
results.overview: In the middle of the Pacific, the Fiji Islands. A village, a community, nestled between ocean and mountains. An island shaken by climate change. Storm clouds loom ahead, while the Fijians remain calm and share a lust for life. Collective strength. Providence. Erasure. Words mingle with the elements, and nature intimately weaves together the relationship between humans and their environment. Two scales, two parallel ways of looking at things, but both speaking with one voice.

results.title: Peripheries
results.overview: Multidisciplinary artist David Hartt (Canadian, born 1967) transforms John Vanderlyn's immersive historical painting, Panoramic View of the Palace and Gardens of Versailles (1818–19), into a dynamic contemporary installation, offering viewers the opportunity to explore questions of place and perspective.
